s: Where was the 12th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC12) held, which reached the first fisheries subsidies deal?
x: MC12 (2022) in Geneva produced the first fisheries subsidies deal.

s: Since which year had the WTO e-commerce moratorium been in place before it lapsed at MC14 in March 2026?
x: The e-commerce moratorium lapsed on 30 March 2026 at MC14 (Yaoundé), the first time since 1998.

s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies entered into force on 15 September 2025 after acceptance by how many members?
x: It entered into force after acceptances by two-thirds (111) of WTO members.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about WTO subsidy boxes?
o: Amber Box support is trade-distorting and capped
Blue Box support is exempt from reduction
The Amber de minimis for developing countries is 10%
Green Box support is capped at 5%
x: Green Box support is unlimited; the 5% de minimis applies to Amber Box support of developed countries.

s: On which issue does the interim 'peace clause' agreed at Bali (2013) protect developing countries?
x: The Bali peace clause shields developing countries breaching de minimis limits on public stockholding for food security.

s: Which country became the 191st member of the IMF on 21 October 2024?
x: Liechtenstein joined as the 191st member with a quota of SDR 100 million.

s: How many member countries does the IBRD have?
x: The IBRD has 189 members, while the IMF has 191.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023?
x: India ranked 38th of 139, up from 44th in 2018 and 54th in 2014.

s: Which lender approved a $788.8 million results-based loan in December 2024 for Amaravati capital Phase-I?
x: The ADB approved $788.8 million and the World Bank $800 million, together about $1.6 billion for Amaravati.

s: What is the size of the World Bank loan for the Amaravati Integrated Urban Development Program?
x: The World Bank approved $800 million on 19 December 2024 (29 years incl. 6-year grace); $207 million was the first tranche.

s: Who is the Managing Director of the IMF?
x: Kristalina Georgieva is the IMF Managing Director.

s: Where was the 13th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC13) held in 2024?
x: MC13 was held in Abu Dhabi (UAE) from 26 February to 2 March 2024; it extended the e-commerce moratorium by two years.

s: What growth rate did the IMF's World Economic Outlook of October 2026 project for India for 2026?
x: The October 2026 WEO projected India's growth at 7.0% for 2026, raised 0.6 point from July.

s: Where was the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14) held in March 2026?
x: MC14 met at Yaoundé, Cameroon in March 2026 and ended in deadlock.

s:
Match the following WTO Ministerial Conferences with their venues:
A. MC12
B. MC13
C. MC14
1. Abu Dhabi
2. Yaoundé
3. Geneva
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: MC12 (2022) was in Geneva, MC13 (2024) in Abu Dhabi and MC14 (2026) in Yaoundé, Cameroon.

s: Which WTO agreement, in force from 15 September 2025, is the WTO's first agreement with environmental sustainability at its core?
x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies bans subsidies to IUU fishing and overfished stocks; it is the WTO's first agreement centred on environmental sustainability.

s: Withdrawal from the Rome Statute of the ICC becomes effective how long after notice to the UN Secretary-General?
x: Withdrawal takes effect one year after notice to the UN Secretary-General.

s: Which grouping did Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, which withdrew from the ICC, form together?
x: The three military-led countries formed the Alliance of Sahel States and called the ICC a 'neo-colonial instrument'.

s: Against whom has an International Criminal Court arrest warrant been pending since March 2023?
x: The ICC arrest warrant against Vladimir Putin has been in force since March 2023.

s: Where is the seat of the International Criminal Court, established in 2002?
x: The ICC, the first permanent international criminal court, sits at The Hague.

s: On which principle does the International Criminal Court work?
x: The ICC works on the principle of complementarity and tries war crimes, crimes against humanity, genocide and aggression.

s: Which was the first permanent international criminal court, established in 2002?
o: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
x: The ICC at The Hague, set up in 2002, is the first permanent international criminal court.

s: Which group has governed Gaza since 2007?
x: Hamas, not the Palestinian Authority, has run Gaza since 2007.

s: Which group was identified among the countries moving towards recognising Palestine at the September 2025 UN General Assembly?
o: Spain, Ireland, Norway, Germany and Austria
Britain, France, Canada, Australia and Belgium
Egypt, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE
Iran, Russia, China, Pakistan and Turkey
x: Britain, France, Canada, Australia and Belgium were identified among the countries moving towards recognition. Spain, Ireland and Norway had already been identified as recognising Palestine, while the other groups are not the specified group in this development.

s: Which European countries were reluctant to recognise Palestine because of their Holocaust legacy?
x: Germany and Austria were reluctant because of their Holocaust legacy; Spain, Ireland and Norway recognised Palestine.

s: In which year did the PLO declare Palestinian statehood?
x: The PLO declared statehood in 1988; 147 of 193 UN members recognise Palestine.

s: Which country hosted the Oslo Accords in 1993?
x: Norway hosted the Oslo Accords in 1993; it is also among the European states that recognised Palestine.

s: How many of the 193 UN members recognise Palestine?
x: 147 of 193 UN members recognise Palestine; the latest before September 2025 was Mexico (January 2025).

s: Which country recognised Palestine in January 2025, the latest before the September 2025 UNGA?
x: Mexico recognised Palestine in January 2025; Spain, Ireland and Norway had recognised earlier.

s: Which country filed a genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice?
x: South Africa brought the genocide case against Israel before the ICJ.

s: A UNESCO assessment in August 2025 recorded damage to how many cultural sites in Gaza?
x: UNESCO recorded damage to 110 cultural sites in Gaza.

s: Which of the following Gaza cultural sites is correctly matched with its historical detail?
o: Church of Saint Porphyrius – Greek Orthodox, 5th century
x: Saint Porphyrius is a 5th-century Greek Orthodox church; the Omari Mosque is 7th century, Al-Qissariya Mamluk and Pasha's Palace a 17th-century Radwan castle.

s: Where was the World Heritage Committee session held at which the Maratha Military Landscapes of India were inscribed in July 2025?
x: They were inscribed on 11 July 2025 at the 47th session in Paris, becoming India's 44th World Heritage property.

s: Which fort of the Maratha Military Landscapes of India is located in Tamil Nadu?
x: The serial nomination has 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu.

s: Which treaty governs the protection of cultural property in armed conflict?
x: The 1954 Hague Convention protects cultural property in armed conflict; Israel is a signatory.

s: Which Gaza site is described as the second-oldest mosque in Palestine?
x: The 7th-century Great Omari Mosque is the second-oldest mosque in Palestine.

s: Which became India's 44th World Heritage property in July 2025?
x: The Maratha Military Landscapes of India were inscribed on 11 July 2025 as India's 44th World Heritage property.

s: How many forts make up the serial nomination 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'?
x: It is a serial nomination of 12 forts: 11 in Maharashtra and Gingee Fort in Tamil Nadu.

s: During Piyush Goyal’s visit to New York on 24 September 2025, which technology was associated with India’s interest in the United States?
x: Piyush Goyal’s New York visit was associated with India’s interest in United States small modular reactor technology. The other technologies were not identified in this context.

s: In which year did India ratify the Convention on Supplementary Compensation for Nuclear Damage?
x: India signed the CSC in 2010 and ratified it in 2016; the India–US civil nuclear deal dates to 2008.

s: In which year was the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act enacted?
x: The CLND Act is of 2010; the Atomic Energy Act is of 1962.

s: At what amount does the SHANTI Act, 2025 cap nuclear liability?
x: The SHANTI Act caps nuclear liability at 300 million SDRs (about ₹3,900 crore).

s: In which year was the India–US civil nuclear deal signed?
x: The India–US civil nuclear deal dates to 2008.

s: Under which law can only state-owned firms such as NPCIL and NTPC run nuclear power plants in India?
o: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
x: The Atomic Energy Act, 1962 allows only state-owned firms to run nuclear plants; it is to be opened to private players.

s: Which section of the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010 deals with supplier liability, which deters foreign suppliers like Westinghouse and Framatome?
x: Section 17(b) of the CLNDA 2010 gives operators a right of recourse against suppliers, which deters foreign suppliers.

s: Which company is developing the 1.8 GW Sawalkote hydroelectric project on the Chenab?
x: Sawalkote is a 1.8 GW NHPC project on the Chenab in Jammu and Kashmir.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sawalkote project and other Chenab developments?
o: Momentum for Sawalkote rose after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty following the Pahalgam attack
The Wullar Barrage was unrelated to this renewed momentum
Dulhasti and Baglihar are other Chenab projects
x: The Wullar Barrage was also associated with the renewed momentum after the treaty's suspension.

s: Though officially termed run-of-river, the Sawalkote project's reservoir (over 50,000 crore litres) is considered closer to which type of project?
x: With a reservoir exceeding 50,000 crore litres, Sawalkote is termed run-of-river but considered closer to a storage project.

s: In which year was the Indus Waters Treaty, suspended by India after the Pahalgam attack, signed?
x: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in 1960; India suspended it after the Pahalgam attack.

s: On which river is the 1.8 GW Sawalkote hydroelectric project in Jammu and Kashmir being built?
x: Sawalkote is an NHPC project on the Chenab, like Dulhasti, Baglihar and Salal.

s: What duty do corn imports into India beyond the tariff-rate quota attract?
x: Imports beyond the quota attract 50% duty, not 25%.

s: Which statement correctly describes India’s position on genetically modified corn in the India–US corn trade dispute?
o: India bans imports of GM corn, while about 94% of US corn in 2024 was GM
India permits all GM corn imports, while about 94% of US corn in 2024 was non-GM
India bans imports of all non-GM corn, while about 94% of US corn in 2024 was GM
India had adopted the NITI Aayog proposal for GM maize for ethanol
x: India bans GM corn imports, and about 94% of US corn in 2024 was genetically modified. The proposal for GM maize for ethanol was withdrawn, so it was not adopted.

s: Which country was India's largest supplier of imported corn in 2024–25?
x: Myanmar supplied 0.53 mt and Ukraine 0.39 mt; the US only 1,100 tonnes.

s: On which day is the enclave exchange day under the 2015 India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement observed?
x: The exchange day was 31 July; 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 Bangladeshi enclaves to India.

s: Under the 2015 Land Boundary Agreement, how many Indian enclaves in Bangladesh were transferred to Bangladesh?
x: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh; 51 Bangladeshi enclaves merged into India.

s: In which district were the 51 Bangladeshi enclaves merged into India under the LBA 2015?
x: The 51 Bangladeshi enclaves were in Cooch Behar, West Bengal.

s: On 18 August 2025, which public-health achievement did the WHO declare for Nepal?
o: Elimination of Congenital Rubella Syndrome globally
Elimination of rubella as a public health problem
Elimination of measles in the WHO South-East Asia Region
x: The WHO declared that Nepal had eliminated rubella as a public health problem. The declaration did not concern global CRS elimination, all vaccine-preventable diseases, or regional measles elimination.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rubella and Nepal?
o: Nepal was first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to adopt a laboratory algorithm for rubella surveillance
The MMR vaccine requires three doses
Rubella is also called German measles
WHO declared Nepal free of rubella as a public health problem in August 2025
x: The MMR vaccine has two doses, not three; the other statements are correct.

s: Rubella (German measles) can cause which condition in infants?
x: Rubella can cause Congenital Rubella Syndrome, with about 1,00,000 cases globally each year.

s: The WHO Pandemic Agreement, adopted in May 2025, needs how many countries for entry into force?
x: It needs 60 countries; the committee vote before adoption was 124 in favour, 0 against, 11 abstentions.

s:
Consider the following statements about the WHO Pandemic Agreement:
1. It was adopted by the World Health Assembly on 20 May 2025.
2. It opened for signature on the day of its adoption.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: It was adopted on 20 May 2025 but opens for signature only after the PABS Annex is adopted.

s: Around the UN's 80th anniversary, who argued that multilateralism is 'wounded, not dead'?
x: Shashi Tharoor described multilateralism as 'wounded, not dead'.

s: UNIFIL, renewed 'for a final time' by UNSC Resolution 2790, is the UN Interim Force in which country?
x: UNIFIL is the UN Interim Force in Lebanon; Resolution 2790 was adopted on 28 August 2025.

s:
Consider the following statements about UNIFIL:
1. It was renewed by UNSC Resolution 2790 in August 2025.
2. Its mandate ended on 31 December 2025.
3. About 10,800 personnel are to withdraw within one year of its mandate end.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Its mandate ends on 31 December 2026, not 2025; withdrawal of about 10,800 personnel follows within one year.

s: China’s K Visa, introduced for young foreign STEM researchers, innovators and entrepreneurs, differs from the R Visa in which respect?
o: Employer sponsorship is not required for the K Visa
Employer sponsorship is mandatory for the K Visa
The K Visa is meant only for high-level foreign experts
The K Visa is meant only for diplomatic personnel
x: Employer sponsorship is not required for China’s K Visa, which targets young foreign STEM talent. The R Visa, in contrast, targets high-level foreign experts and requires employer sponsorship.

s: China’s K Visa for young foreign STEM talent was announced in the context of which development in the United States?
o: It was announced alongside the United States introducing the R Visa
It was announced weeks after the United States raised the H-1B fee by $100,000
It was announced weeks before the United States raised the H-1B fee by $100,000
It was announced after the United States ended employer sponsorship for the H-1B visa
x: China announced the K Visa weeks before the United States raised the H-1B fee by $100,000. The announcement therefore preceded, rather than followed, that United States measure.

s: Which combination is associated with China’s effort to attract and develop STEM talent?
o: The slogan “New Quality Productive Forces” and the ASEAN Community Vision 2045
The slogan “New Quality Productive Forces” and the Thousand Talents Programme
The slogan “Thousand Talents Programme” and the H-1B fee increase
The slogan “ASEAN Community Vision 2045” and the Thousand Talents Programme
x: Xi Jinping used the slogan “New Quality Productive Forces,” while the Thousand Talents Programme is also associated with China’s talent strategy. The other combinations incorrectly treat a programme or a separate regional vision as the slogan.

s: The India–ILO MoU, rooted in India's 2023 G20 presidency, concerns the development of which of the following?
x: India and the ILO agreed to develop the International Reference Classification of Occupations (IRCO), following the G20's 2023 endorsement of skills-based migration pathways.

s: The US H-1B visa is an example of which type of migration seen since the 1990s?
x: Skilled migration has existed since the 1990s, the US H-1B being an example; GCC countries host mainly temporary labour migrants.

s: The PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana targets how many formal jobs in two years?
x: The Yojana targets 35 million formal jobs in two years.

s: In September 2025, the Trump administration raised the fee for new H-1B visa applicants to what amount?
x: The fee for new H-1B applicants was raised to $100,000, approximately six times the earlier fee. The tempting option $85,000 refers to the annual H-1B quota, not the visa fee.

s: Who was the ILO Director-General who signed the IRCO MoU with India in Geneva?
x: The MoU was signed by Ambassador Arindam Bagchi and ILO DG Gilbert F. Houngbo.

s: What is the annual US H-1B quota, in place since 2004?
x: The H-1B quota is 85,000 a year, including 20,000 for US advanced degrees.

s: Which of the following diaspora category–legal basis pairs is correctly matched?
x: The NRI's legal basis includes the Income Tax Act, 1961 (and FEMA, 1999); the PIO's basis was the PIO Card Scheme, 2002.

s: How large is the Indian diaspora, and whom does it comprise?
o: 32 million or more, comprising only NRIs
Less than 32 million, comprising PIOs and NRIs
32 million or more, comprising PIOs and NRIs
Less than 32 million, comprising only PIOs
x: The Indian diaspora was placed at 32 million or more and includes both Persons of Indian Origin and Non-Resident Indians. The alternatives alter either the size or the categories included.

s: Which of the following statements regarding India's diaspora-related citizenship provisions is incorrect?
o: The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003 created OCI through Sections 7A–7D.
The PIO and OCI schemes were merged in 2015.
An NRI is Indian, whereas a PIO is foreign.
x: The incorrect statement is that India permits dual citizenship; India does not permit dual citizenship. The other statements correctly describe the creation of OCI, the 2015 PIO–OCI merger and the citizenship distinction between NRIs and PIOs.

s: Which category among the following can vote in person under the stated distinction between NRIs and PIOs?
x: An NRI can vote in person, whereas a PIO cannot. OCI is a citizenship-related status and the Know India Programme is a platform, not the category identified as having this voting provision.

s: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)?
x: UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya.

s: Where is the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) headquartered?
x: WMO, like WHO, ITU, WTO and ILO, is headquartered in Geneva.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: IAEA is headed by Rafael Grossi. Arsenio Dominguez is the Secretary-General of the IMO, headquartered in London.

s: Which is the oldest UN agency, established in 1865?
x: The ITU, founded in 1865, is the oldest UN agency; it has 194 members and is headquartered in Geneva, not London.

s: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus belongs to which country?
x: Tedros is Ethiopian. Celeste Saulo is Argentine, Arsenio Dominguez Panamanian and Qu Dongyu Chinese.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
x: Gilbert F. Houngbo is from Togo, not Ghana. The other three institutional leadership-nationality pairs are correctly matched.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
x: The IMF formally came into existence on 27 December 1945, while its operations began on 1 March 1947.

s: The 36-member Council is associated with which organisation?
x: ICAO, established in 1944 under the Chicago Convention, has a 36-member Council and is headquartered in Montreal.

s: Where is the UNFCCC Secretariat located?
x: The UNFCCC secretariat is in Bonn, with 198 Parties.

s: Where is the secretariat of the International Solar Alliance located?
x: The ISA secretariat is at Gurugram; New Delhi hosts CDRI.

s: In which year was the Bretton Woods Conference held?
x: The Bretton Woods Conference took place in 1944. Its ideas were associated with Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes.

s: Khaled El-Enany, who became UNESCO Director-General in November 2025, belongs to which country?
x: El-Enany, an Egyptian Egyptologist, is UNESCO's first Arab head; he succeeded Audrey Azoulay of France.

s: Where was the 43rd UNESCO General Conference held, which elected Khaled El-Enany as Director-General?
x: He was elected on 6 November 2025 by the 43rd General Conference at Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

s: Gilbert F. Houngbo, Director-General of the ILO, belongs to which country?
x: The ILO head Houngbo is from Togo, not Ghana.

s: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the WTO, belongs to which country?
x: The WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is Nigerian.

s: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva belongs to which country?
x: Georgieva is Bulgarian; Rebeca Grynspan (UNCTAD) is from Costa Rica and Grossi and Saulo are Argentine.

s: Which UN agency is headquartered in London?
x: IMO is in London; ITU and WMO are in Geneva and ICAO in Montreal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UNESCO?
o: It has 194 members and 12 associate members.
Khaled El-Enany succeeded Audrey Azoulay as its head.
x: UNESCO's Executive Board has 58 members; the 36-member Council belongs to ICAO.

s: Where is the headquarters of INTERPOL?
x: INTERPOL is headquartered at Lyon, France.

s: Which two countries set up the UN Alliance of Civilizations in 2005?
x: The UN Alliance of Civilizations (New York) was set up in 2005 by Türkiye and Spain.

s: Who was the first African to become Director-General of the WHO, in 2017?
x: Tedros of Ethiopia became WHO DG in 2017, succeeding Margaret Chan, the first African to head the WHO.

s: Who is the President of the World Bank?
x: Ajay Banga, an Indian-born US national, is President of the World Bank.

s: Where is the headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)?
x: ICAO, created by the Chicago Convention (1944), is headquartered in Montreal.

s: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 was based on the ideas of which two economists?
o: Harry Dexter White and John Maynard Keynes
x: The Bretton Woods institutions grew from the plans of Harry Dexter White (US) and John Maynard Keynes (UK).

s: Who was Managing Director of the IMF from 2011 to 2019 and later became President of the European Central Bank?
x: Christine Lagarde headed the IMF in 2011-2019 and then became ECB President; Georgieva succeeded her.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: New Development Bank — Chair in 2026: Uzbekistan
x: Bangladesh is the BIMSTEC chair for 2026. The other pairings incorrectly assign leadership roles not stated for those organisations.

s: Which of the following countries joined BRICS from 1 January 2024?
o: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates
Argentina, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia and Egypt
Ethiopia, Saudi Arabia, Indonesia and the United Arab Emirates
x: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates joined BRICS from 1 January 2024. Argentina declined the invitation, while Indonesia joined in 2025 and Saudi Arabia's status remained unconfirmed.

s: Where is the Secretariat of APEC located?
x: APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat is in Singapore; India is only an observer.

s: Which country was invited to join BRICS at Johannesburg in August 2023 but declined?
x: Argentina declined; Egypt and Ethiopia joined on 1 January 2024 and Indonesia in January 2025.

s: Which country became NATO's 32nd member in 2024?
x: Sweden joined as the 32nd member in 2024; Finland had joined as the 31st in 2023.

s: Which country became the 10th member of the New Development Bank and its first from Central Asia?
x: Uzbekistan became the NDB's 10th member and the first from Central Asia; the NDB is headquartered in Shanghai.

s: Which country joined the New Development Bank (NDB) in 2023?
x: Egypt joined the NDB (set up by the 2014 Fortaleza Declaration, HQ Shanghai) in 2023. Uzbekistan later became the 10th member and first from Central Asia. Argentina and Indonesia are BRICS-expansion names, not NDB entrants.

s: Which of the following is a Maastricht criterion for entry into the Eurozone?
x: Eurozone entry criteria include a fiscal deficit below 3% of GDP, debt below 60% of GDP and participation in ERM II.

s: Which country became the 21st member of the Eurozone?
x: Bulgaria became the Eurozone's 21st member.

s: What is India's status in APEC?
x: APEC has 21 economies and its Secretariat in Singapore; India is not a member, only an observer.

s: In which year did the African Union become a member of the G20?
x: The G20 has 19 countries, the EU and the African Union, which joined in 2023.

s: Which country joined BRICS in January 2025?
x: Indonesia joined in January 2025. Egypt joined in 2024, Argentina declined and Saudi Arabia has not formally joined.

s: Which country became the 119th member of the International Solar Alliance?
x: Malta became the 119th member of the ISA.

s: Where was the APEC summit of 2025 held?
x: The 2025 APEC summit was held at Gyeongju, South Korea, where China proposed WAICO.

s: Deepavali was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in December 2025 as India's which element?
x: Deepavali became India's 16th ICH element on 10 December 2025; 45 is Sarnath's World Heritage number.

s: Where was the 20th session of UNESCO's Intergovernmental Committee on Intangible Heritage (December 2025) held?
x: The 20th session met at the Red Fort, New Delhi (8-13 December 2025), the first time India hosted it.

s: Which Indian city joined the UNESCO Creative Cities Network for Gastronomy in 2025?
x: Lucknow joined in 2025 as India's second Gastronomy city; Hyderabad was the first, in 2019.

s: Which of the following pairs (UNESCO Creative City – field) is correctly matched?
x: Kozhikode is a City of Literature (2023). Gwalior is Music, Mumbai Film and Srinagar Crafts and Folk Arts.

s: Where is the Exploration Museum with an Astronaut Monument honouring Apollo astronauts?
x: The Exploration Museum at Húsavík, Iceland, tells the history of exploration; its Astronaut Monument (2015) honours 32 Apollo astronauts.

s: In which country is the Makli necropolis, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, located?
x: Makli necropolis, near Thatta in Sindh, Pakistan, is one of the world's largest and a World Heritage Site since 1981.

s: Sarnath became India's which numbered World Heritage Site in July 2026?
x: Sarnath became India's 45th World Heritage Site in July 2026.

s: Which organisations jointly sponsor the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)?
x: The IPCC is sponsored by UNEP and WMO. Its AR6 synthesis report was released on 20 March 2023, and its AR7 cycle began in July 2023.

s: Which organisation sponsors the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, known as the “Seed Treaty”?
x: The ITPGRFA is sponsored by FAO and concerns plant genetic resources in harmony with the Convention on Biological Diversity.

s: The ‘Great Reset’ is an initiative of which organisation?
x: The Great Reset was a World Economic Forum initiative launched in 2020.

s: Which of the following INTERPOL notices is correctly matched with its purpose?
o: Blue Notice – Locate and arrest a wanted person pending extradition
Silver Notice – Information on a person's identity, location or activities
x: The Yellow Notice is for missing persons. Red is to locate and arrest pending extradition, Blue seeks information on identity/location, and Silver (2025) traces criminal assets.

s:
Which of the following international roles are associated with India in 2026?
1. Chair of the Kimberley Process
2. Host of ITU PP-30
3. Founder of ISA, CDRI and GBA
x: India chairs the Kimberley Process in 2026, is to host ITU PP-30 and is a founder of the ISA, CDRI and GBA.

s: What is the Colombo Process?
o: A regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries on overseas employment
An INTERPOL system for tracing criminal assets
A WEF initiative on global economic restructuring
A UN mechanism for electing non-permanent members
x: The Colombo Process is a regional forum of Asian labour-sending countries concerned with overseas employment.

s: Which country is the sixth member of the Colombo Security Conclave, formed in 2020?
x: The Conclave comprises India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius, Bangladesh and Seychelles, with Seychelles as the 6th member. Bangladesh is a member but not the sixth; Myanmar and Indonesia are not members.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kimberley Process — conflict-diamond certification — no headquarters
Global Biofuels Alliance — India's G20 — biofuels
x: CDRI was sponsored by India in 2019 and is headquartered in New Delhi. Japan and Tokyo are not its sponsor and secretariat combination.

s: Where is the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure (CDRI) headquartered?
x: CDRI, launched by India in 2019, is headquartered in New Delhi, not Tokyo; Gurugram hosts the ISA.

s: What does the U.S.-led 'Pax Silica', which India joined in February 2026, concern?
o: Maritime security in the Indian Ocean
Critical minerals, semiconductor and AI supply chains
x: Pax Silica covers critical minerals, semiconductor and AI supply chains; energy resilience is the aim of Japan's POWERR Asia.

s: POWERR Asia, launched under AZEC Plus in April 2026, is an initiative of which country?
x: POWERR Asia is Japan's initiative under AZEC Plus for energy resilience; India is a participant.

s: In India, which agency serves as the INTERPOL National Central Bureau?
x: The CBI is India's INTERPOL National Central Bureau and seeks Red Notices.

s: Which INTERPOL notice, the newest one introduced in 2025, is used to identify and trace criminal assets?
x: The Silver Notice (2025) is the newest INTERPOL notice and is used to trace criminal assets.

s: At which meeting was the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance for 2026–2036 adopted?
x: The 79th World Health Assembly, held in May 2026, adopted the Global Action Plan on AMR 2026–2036.

s: In the WHO Pandemic Agreement negotiations, India backs which grouping?
x: India backs the developing-country Group for Equity in the negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement.

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Fiji — 26th country to eliminate trachoma, October 2025
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014, not malaria-free. Cabo Verde, Fiji and Sri Lanka are correctly matched with the stated certifications.

s: Which country was the first in the Americas to eliminate leprosy?
x: WHO certified Chile as the first country in the Americas to eliminate leprosy.

s: In which year was India certified polio-free?
x: India was certified polio-free in 2014; 2016 is Sri Lanka's malaria-free year.

s: On which date was the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted?
x: The Agreement was adopted on 20 May 2025; talks on its PABS annex resumed in Geneva in July 2026.

s: In October 2025, Fiji became the 26th country to eliminate which disease?
x: Fiji was certified the 26th country to eliminate trachoma, its first NTD eliminated.

s: Which country became the first in Africa to end onchocerciasis (river blindness)?
x: Niger became the first in Africa and fifth in the world to end onchocerciasis, in late 2025.

s: Which country was most recently certified malaria-free by WHO, in July 2025?
x: Timor-Leste was certified malaria-free in July 2025; Cabo Verde in 2024 and Sri Lanka in 2016.

s: In which countries is wild poliovirus now endemic?
x: Wild poliovirus is endemic only in Pakistan and Afghanistan; India was certified polio-free in 2014.

s: What does the still-unfinished annex of the WHO Pandemic Agreement deal with?
x: The PABS (Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing) annex is unfinished; talks resumed in Geneva in July 2026.

s: Which country became the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies?
x: Bhutan became the first in the WHO South-East Asia Region to eliminate dog-transmitted rabies (September 2026).

s: Which organisations are headed respectively by Rafael Grossi and Rebeca Grynspan, candidates for UN Secretary-General in 2026?
x: Rafael Grossi is Director General of the IAEA and Rebeca Grynspan is Secretary-General of UNCTAD.

s: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host which event in 2030?
o: World Summit on the Information Society
x: The ITU Council accepted India's bid to host the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2030, known as PP-30.

s: India took over the chairmanship of the Kimberley Process on 1 January 2026 for which time?
x: India, a founding member, took over the chair on 1 January 2026 for the third time; the Process has 60 participants (59 countries and the EU).

s: Under Article 97 of the UN Charter, who appoints the UN Secretary-General?
o: The Economic and Social Council on the recommendation of the Security Council
The UN Security Council on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The International Court of Justice on the recommendation of the General Assembly
The UN General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council
x: Article 97 provides for appointment by the UN General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

s: Khalilur Rahman, elected President of the 81st UN General Assembly (2026-27), is from which country?
x: Khalilur Rahman of Bangladesh was elected in the Asia-Pacific Group's turn, defeating the candidate from Cyprus.

s: On which date does the five-year term of the next UN Secretary-General begin?
x: Guterres demits office at the end of 2026 and his successor's term begins on 1 January 2027.

s: Which term is India's election to the UN Human Rights Council for 2026-28?
x: India was elected unopposed to the UNHRC for 2026-28, its 7th term.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the U.S. exit from international bodies announced in January 2026?
o: It included the UNFCCC, IPCC and IRENA
The U.S. was described as the first country to attempt formal withdrawal from the UNFCCC
UN Women and UNFPA were among the bodies exited
The International Solar Alliance was not among the bodies exited
x: The ISA was among the bodies the U.S. exited, along with UNFPA, UN Women, UNHRC and UNCTAD.

s: When did the UN Security Council hold its first-ever meeting on the risks posed by artificial intelligence to international peace?
x: The first UNSC meeting on AI risks to peace was held in July 2023 (asked before). The other dates are distractors with no such first meeting.

s: UNMISS is the UN peacekeeping mission in which country?
x: UNMISS is in South Sudan; MONUSCO is in DR Congo, UNIFIL in Lebanon and MINURSO in Western Sahara.

s: Which UN peacekeeping mission is the referendum mission in Western Sahara?
x: MINURSO is the Western Sahara referendum mission; UNDOF is on the Golan Heights and UNFICYP in Cyprus.

s: Which UN peacekeeping mission ended after the host country withdrew consent in June 2023?
x: MINUSMA is no longer active because Mali withdrew consent in June 2023.

s: For which term was India re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board in December 2025?
x: India was re-elected to the UNESCO Executive Board for 2025-29; 2025-28 is its ICAO Council term and 2026-28 its UNHRC term.

s: The Kimberley Process, chaired by India in 2026, has how many participants?
x: The Kimberley Process has 60 participants: 59 countries plus the EU.

s: A candidate for UN Secretary-General needs how many 'encourage' votes in the UNSC, with no P5 veto?
x: A candidate needs 9 'encourage' votes and no veto from a permanent member.

s:
Match the following UN peacekeeping missions with their host areas:
A. MONUSCO
B. UNDOF
C. UNFICYP
D. UNMISS
1. Cyprus
2. South Sudan
3. DR Congo
4. Golan Heights
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: MONUSCO is in DR Congo, UNDOF on the Golan Heights, UNFICYP in Cyprus and UNMISS in South Sudan.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hague Conventions (HCCH) – UK–EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
x: The Stockholm Convention (2001) covers persistent organic pollutants. Chicago is civil aviation, HCCH is private international law and the Windsor Framework covers Northern Ireland trade rules.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Basel Convention — prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
x: The Vienna Convention of 1985 concerns protection of the ozone layer. Rotterdam concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste, and the Windsor Framework concerns post-Brexit UK–EU trade rules for Northern Ireland.

s: Which convention governs the transboundary movement of hazardous waste?
x: The Basel Convention of 1989 governs transboundary hazardous waste. It also includes a plastic-waste amendment and stronger rules relating to e-waste.

s: In which year was the Basel Convention adopted?
x: The Basel Convention dates from 1989, after the Chicago Convention (1944) and before Stockholm (2001) and Minamata (2013).

s: On which date did the BBNJ (High Seas) Treaty enter into force?
x: Adopted in March 2023, the BBNJ Treaty entered into force on 17 January 2026; India has signed but not ratified it.

s: What does the Minamata Convention (2013) deal with?
x: The Minamata Convention concerns mercury, with dental amalgam to be phased out by 2034; POPs belong to the Stockholm Convention.

s: Which country became the first South Asian party to the UN Water Convention (Helsinki, 1992)?
x: Bangladesh became the first South Asian party to the Water Convention, which governs transboundary rivers and lakes.

s:
With reference to the five UN outer-space treaties, consider the following:
1. India has ratified the Moon Agreement of 1979.
2. India has signed all five treaties.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: India has signed all five and ratified four; the exception is the 1979 Moon Agreement, which India has not ratified.

s: In whose name are treaties concluded in India?
x: Treaties concluded by India are concluded in the name of the President. Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate for their implementation.

s: What does Article 253 of the Constitution of India enable Parliament to do?
o: appoint the secretariat of every UN convention
ratify every treaty without executive action
withdraw India from any treaty without consultation
legislate for implementing treaties and international agreements
x: Article 253 empowers Parliament to make laws for implementing treaties, agreements and conventions with foreign countries or decisions made at international conferences.

s: India's refusal to join which of the following has been defended as protecting its policy space?
o: The IFD initiative and the WHO Pandemic Agreement
The UN Cybercrime Convention and the WHO Pandemic Agreement
The IFD initiative and the UN Cybercrime Convention
x: India's refusals on Investment Facilitation for Development and the Cybercrime Convention are defended as protecting policy space; the Pandemic Agreement is a separate matter.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UN Convention against Cybercrime?
o: It is the first global cybercrime treaty, adopted in December 2024
It becomes binding 90 days after 40 ratifications
It was opened for signature at Hanoi in October 2025
x: The Convention's secretariat is UNODC, not UNCTAD.

s: Under the Kigali Amendment, beyond which date will India stop clearances for new HFC production?
x: India will stop clearances for new hydrofluorocarbon production beyond 31 December 2027 under the Kigali Amendment.

s: When did a joint Congress at Versailles approve France's constitutional guarantee of abortion freedom?
x: The joint Congress at Versailles approved it on 4 March 2024 (780-72).

s: What does the Windsor Framework (2023) concern?
o: UK-EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland
x: The Windsor Framework sets UK-EU post-Brexit trade rules for Northern Ireland.

s: Which instrument on ozone-depleting substances has been universally ratified by 197 parties?
x: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is universally ratified (197); Stockholm covers POPs, Rotterdam prior informed consent and Basel hazardous waste.

s: What does the Rotterdam Convention deal with?
o: Prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals
x: Rotterdam = prior informed consent; Stockholm = POPs; Minamata = mercury; Vienna/Montreal = ozone.

s: The Apostille Convention (1961) is one of the conventions of which body?
o: Hague Conference on Private International Law
x: The Hague Conventions (HCCH) cover private international law, including the Apostille (1961) and Child Abduction (1980) conventions.

s: What is India's status on the BBNJ (High Seas) Treaty?
x: India has signed but not ratified the BBNJ Treaty, which entered into force on 17 January 2026.

s: Which was the first country to explicitly guarantee the freedom to have an abortion in its Constitution?
x: France did so through a joint Congress at Versailles on 4 March 2024 (vote 780-72).

s: Between which two countries were the US-brokered Washington Accords signed on 4 December 2025?
x: The Washington Accords of 4 December 2025 were a US-brokered peace deal between the DRC and Rwanda.

s: Under whose chairmanship did the European Convention draft the EU Constitution, which failed in the 2005 referendums?
x: The European Convention under Valery Giscard d'Estaing drafted the EU Constitution; after it failed in 2005, the Lisbon Treaty (2009) replaced it.

s: By which year does the Minamata Convention require dental amalgam to be phased out?
x: The Minamata Convention (2013) on mercury provides for phasing out dental amalgam by 2034.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about criticisms of the WTO and the Bretton Woods institutions?
o: The WTO Appellate Body is paralysed.
India is blocking the Investment Facilitation for Development (IFD) agreement.
A voting imbalance continues in the Bretton Woods institutions.
The Bretton Woods institutions have abolished quota-based voting.
x: Quota-based voting has not been abolished; the criticism is a continuing voting imbalance. Appellate Body paralysis and India's blocking of IFD are correct.

s:
Consider the following statements about the India-Oman CEPA:
1. It provides duty-free treatment for 99% of India's exports.
2. It is India's first CEPA with a GCC country.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: The India-Oman CEPA (signed December 2025, in force June 2026) makes 99% of India's exports duty-free; it is India's second GCC CEPA, not the first.

s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium lapsed in March 2026 after the failure of which Ministerial Conference?
x: The failure of MC14 and the lapse of the e-commerce moratorium were reported in March 2026.

s: In which years was the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) signed and brought into force respectively?
x: GATT was signed in 1947 and entered into force in 1948.

s: Which trade agreement has been described as the 'Mother of All Deals'?
x: The India-EU FTA is called the 'Mother of All Deals'; the India-UK CETA is the 'Gold standard' deal.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: India signed the CEPA with the UAE in 2022. ECTA was with Australia, TEPA with EFTA and CETA with the UK.

s: Which WTO subsidy box covers trade-distorting domestic support that is subject to a cap based on de minimis limits?
x: Amber Box subsidies are trade-distorting domestic support measures and are subject to prescribed limits, including de minimis ceilings.

s: Support tied to production-limiting programmes is classified under which WTO subsidy box?
x: Blue Box support is linked to programmes that limit production.

s: Under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture, which measures fall in the Green Box?
o: Have minimal or no trade-distorting effect
Relate exclusively to intellectual property rights
Are subject to annual reduction commitments
Are capped at a fixed share of production value
x: Green Box support has minimal or no trade distortion and is not capped; IPRs fall under TRIPS.

s: What is TRIMs concerned with?
x: TRIMs refers to Trade-Related Investment Measures.

s: On which date did the WTO, created by the Uruguay Round, come into existence?
x: The Uruguay Round (eighth GATT round, begun 1986) led to the WTO on 1 January 1995.

s: The Peace Clause agreed at Bali in 2013 mainly protects developing countries from WTO disputes on which issue?
x: The Bali Peace Clause shields developing countries' public food-stockholding programmes from disputes over Amber Box limits until a permanent solution is found.

s: Which of the following developments was identified as weakening multilateralism?
o: The failure of MC14 and withdrawals by the United States
The creation of the World Development Report
The launch of the SDR basket
The success of MC14 and the expansion of the Appellate Body
x: The failure of MC14 and U.S. exits were identified as developments weakening multilateralism.

s: Where was the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference (March 2026) held?
x: MC14 met at Yaoundé, Cameroon, on 26-29 March 2026 and ended in deadlock.

s: The Dunkel Draft (1991) was put forward during which GATT round?
x: GATT Director-General Arthur Dunkel's proposals came during the Uruguay Round.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Uruguay Round:
1. It was the 8th GATT round.
2. The Marrakesh Agreement was signed on 1 January 1995.
3. It concluded on 15 December 1993.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Marrakesh Agreement was signed on 15 April 1994; 1 January 1995 is when the WTO came into being.

s: Which pair (India's trade agreement – partner) is correctly matched?
x: The ECTA is with Australia. TEPA is with EFTA, CETA with the UK and the 2022 CEPA with the UAE.

s: How many FTAs did India have, and covering how many countries, as of June 2026?
x: India had 15 FTAs covering 27 countries as of June 2026.

s: The India-EU FTA is to operate along with which agreements?
o: An Investment Protection Agreement and a GI Agreement
A GI Agreement and a Nuclear Liability Convention
An Investment Protection Agreement and a Nuclear Liability Convention
x: The India-EU FTA ('Mother of All Deals') comes with an Investment Protection Agreement and a Geographical Indications Agreement; no nuclear liability convention accompanies it.

s: Which lenders finance the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System?
x: The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS is associated with NDB financing in collaboration with ADB and serves the National Capital Region.

s: Which combination best describes the structural adjustment programmes of the 1980s and 1990s?
o: Debt cancellation, disarmament and refugee resettlement
Public food stocking, tariff abolition and gold accumulation
Universal subsidies, nationalisation and currency appreciation
x: Structural adjustment programmes commonly involved austerity, privatisation and devaluation; studies linked them to rising poverty and inequality in the Global South.

s: What is IMF lending mainly intended to address?
x: The IMF lends only to members, mainly for balance-of-payments problems; the Rapid Financing Instrument gives quick liquidity without a full programme.

s: What is the BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement intended to provide?
o: IMF-type liquidity support for BRICS members
x: The BRICS Contingency Reserve Arrangement provides BRICS members an alternative to IMF liquidity support.

s: Which of the following is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group?
x: The International Finance Corporation is the private-sector arm of the World Bank Group and has 184 members.

s:
Assertion (A): The IMF's SDR basket consists of five currencies.
Reason (R): The Chinese yuan is not part of the SDR basket.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is true: the basket comprises the US dollar, euro, Chinese yuan, Japanese yen and pound sterling. R is false because the yuan is included.

s: Which of the following pairs about BRICS and IMF voting is correctly matched?
o: BRICS share of IMF votes in 2011 – about 20%
BRICS current share of world GDP – about 20%
BRICS share of world GDP in 2011 – about 20%
BRICS current IMF vote share – roughly double the 2011 share
x: In 2011 BRICS had about 20% of world GDP but only 11% of IMF votes; it now has about 40% of GDP with a vote share only barely higher.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB):
1. It was established in 2016.
2. It has 111 approved members.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: AIIB was established in 2016 and has 111 approved members.

s: What are the World Bank road and school projects in Andhra Pradesh called?
x: The World Bank road and school projects in Andhra Pradesh are referred to as SALT projects.

s: Approximately how much was facilitated by the Centre for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO?
x: The Centre facilitated approximately ₹26,000 crore for Amaravati through the World Bank, ADB and HUDCO; ₹15,000 crore was separately fast-tracked as special assistance.

s: Which country was the first borrower from the International Monetary Fund?
x: France was the first country to borrow from the IMF.

s: After the 2010 reforms, what is India's voting share in the IMF?
x: India's IMF voting share is about 2.63%; its quota share is about 2.75%.

s: Which IMF reserve asset is called 'paper gold'?
x: The SDR, valued on a basket of five currencies, is known as 'paper gold'.

s: Which IMF facility gives quick liquidity without a full programme for disasters, pandemics or post-conflict needs?
x: The Rapid Financing Instrument provides quick liquidity without a full programme; the CRA is a BRICS arrangement.

s:
Consider the following statements about the New Development Bank:
1. It was set up under the Fortaleza Declaration of 2014.
2. It is headquartered in Shanghai.
3. Its founder members each hold a veto.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The NDB gives no country a veto; the founders' vote only cannot fall below 55%.

s: In which state are the Mission Schools of Excellence, financed by the AIIB and the World Bank?
x: AIIB and the World Bank fund Gujarat's ₹7,500-crore Mission Schools of Excellence.

s: Which arm of the World Bank Group gives zero- or low-interest loans and grants to the world's poorest countries?
x: IDA is the World Bank's concessional arm; it gives zero- or low-interest loans (credits) and grants to the poorest countries.

s: In which year was the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank Group set up?
x: IDA was set up in 1960; the IFC came in 1956 and MIGA in 1988.

s: The World Bank financed the Gazipur-Elenga (N4) and Natore-Nawabganj (N6) road-safety highways in which country?
x: In June 2023 the World Bank approved $358 million for Bangladesh's N4 and N6 highway road-safety projects.

s: Foreign direct investment inflows in 2025 increased by 73% to about how much?
x: FDI inflows increased by 73% in 2025 to approximately $47 billion.

s: Who publishes the Global Investment Trends Monitor?
x: The Global Investment Trends Monitor is a UNCTAD publication; it reported India's FDI rising 73% to $47 billion in 2025.

s: To which grade did S&P upgrade India's sovereign rating from BBB- in 2025?
x: S&P raised India from BBB- to BBB in 2025, its first upgrade in nearly two decades, and affirmed BBB in September 2026.

s: India's growth during the period under consideration was driven mainly by which combination?
o: Foreign aid and reduction in public investment
Strong private consumption and public investment
x: The principal growth drivers identified were strong private consumption and public investment.

s: India became the world's fourth-largest economy in 2025 in nominal GDP, with a size of about how much?
x: India was reported as the fourth-largest economy in 2025 with a nominal GDP of approximately $4.18 trillion, overtaking Japan.

s: What was India's position in the IMF ranking after the fall in the rupee?
x: India was reported to have slipped to sixth place in the IMF ranking after the rupee's fall.

s: Which country was India's largest import source in 2024–25 among the following?
x: China was India's largest listed import source in 2024–25, accounting for 15.73%, followed by Russia, the UAE and the United States.

s: What were India's record remittances in FY 2024–25?
x: India received record remittances of approximately $135 billion in FY 2024–25.

s: Which institution projected India's growth at 6.6 per cent for 2026-27 in June 2026?
x: The Reserve Bank of India projected India's growth at 6.6 per cent for 2026-27 in June 2026.

s: Which organisation has published the World Investment Report since 1991?
x: The World Investment Report has been published by the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development since 1991.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The World Economic Outlook is an IMF report. Global Economic Prospects, World Development Report and Human Capital Index are associated with the World Bank.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The World Bank's Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June.
2. World Development Report 2025, 'Standards for Development', is an IMF report.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Global Economic Prospects is issued in January and June (India's FY26 forecast raised from 6.3% to 7.2%); the World Development Report is a World Bank report.

s: In January 2026, to what did the IMF raise India's 2025-26 growth projection?
x: The IMF's January 2026 WEO raised FY26 to 7.3% (from 6.6%); 6.2% was its April 2026 FY27 figure and 7.2% the World Bank's January figure.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Corruption Perceptions Index — World Economic Forum
Travel and Tourism Development Index — Transparency International
x: The Logistics Performance Index is published by the World Bank. The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by Transparency International, while the Global Gender Gap and Travel and Tourism Development indices are associated with the World Economic Forum.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023?
x: India was 38th of 139 countries in the LPI 2023.

s: Who publishes the World Economic Outlook?
x: WEO is the IMF's report; Global Economic Prospects is the World Bank's and the World Investment Report UNCTAD's.

s: According to the WTO, what was India's rank as an exporter of commercial services in 2024?
x: India was the 8th-largest exporter (4.3%) and 9th-largest importer (3.4%) of commercial services in 2024.

s: How many members does the OECD, headquartered in Paris, have?
x: The OECD has its headquarters in Paris and has 38 members.

s: Which organisation publishes the Global Gender Gap Report?
x: The Global Gender Gap and the Travel and Tourism Development reports are published by the World Economic Forum.

s: What are the official languages of Belgium?
x: Belgium's languages are Dutch, French and German, not English; its capital is Brussels.

s: Giorgia Meloni is notable for which of the following?
o: She became Italy’s first woman Prime Minister and its longest continuously serving post-war Prime Minister.
She became Nepal’s youngest Prime Minister.
She was Japan’s first woman Prime Minister.
She became Venezuela’s first interim President.
x: Giorgia Meloni is Italy’s first woman Prime Minister and became the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy’s post-war history.

s: Which of the following was a focus of the 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group on Tourism Cooperation?
x: Destination twinning was among the focus areas of the 2nd India–Italy Joint Working Group on Tourism Cooperation. The other options are unrelated to the tourism cooperation agenda identified for the meeting.

s: During the India–Belgium talks in New Delhi, what target was set for bilateral trade?
o: To increase it by 50% in three years
To double it in five years
To maintain it at the existing level for five years
x: India and Belgium aimed to double bilateral trade in five years. The alternatives change either the target or the time period; the defence Letter of Intent was a separate outcome of the talks.

s: Which of the following about Italy's 2026 school policy on full-face coverings is NOT correct?
o: It bans full-face coverings in schools.
Foreign students lacking Italian are limited to 30% of first-year classes.
x: The fines range from €200 to €1,000, not €100 to €500.

s: In the context of India–Belgium cooperation, which pair is correctly matched?
o: Green ammonia project – Link between imec and India
x: Zorawar is a light tank. The green ammonia project is linked to Kakinada and semiconductor cooperation to linking imec with India.

s: In which year did India and Italy establish a Strategic Partnership?
x: The India-Italy Strategic Partnership dates to 2023; diplomatic ties go back to 1947.

s: The green ammonia project at Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh) was an area of cooperation in India's talks with which country?
x: PM Modi and Belgian PM Bart De Wever discussed the Kakinada green ammonia project, the Zorawar light tank and critical minerals.

s: Which Canadian Prime Minister agreed with PM Narendra Modi in October 2026 to expand the India-Canada strategic partnership?
x: PM Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney agreed to expand cooperation in trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.

s: In which year did India and Canada establish diplomatic relations?
x: India-Canada diplomatic relations date from 1947; Canada supplies uranium, pulses and farm products to India.

s: Exercise Konkan-2026, held 8-15 October 2026 off Plymouth, Britain, is a bilateral naval exercise between India and which country?
x: Konkan is the annual bilateral exercise of the Indian Navy and the UK Royal Navy; the 2026 edition was held off Plymouth.

s: Which Talwar-class frigate represented India in Exercise Konkan-2026?
x: INS Trishul, a Talwar-class frigate, took part in Konkan-2026; INS Sahyadri is Shivalik-class.

s: Where was the India-UAE exercise Mountain Guardian-2026 (5-18 October 2026) held?
x: Mountain Guardian-2026 was held at the Chaubatia Foreign Training Centre in Uttarakhand, with a focus on mountain warfare.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the India-UAE exercise Mountain Guardian-2026?
o: 92 personnel took part, 46 from each side
India was represented by the Bhairav Battalion
Women officers and female combat personnel took part
x: The focus of Mountain Guardian-2026 was mountain warfare, not desert warfare.

s: Which Indian Navy ship took part in the India-Russia naval exercise INDRA-2026 at Vladivostok?
x: The Shivalik-class stealth frigate INS Sahyadri took part in INDRA-2026, held 13-18 October in Vladivostok and the Sea of Japan.

s: Vladivostok, venue of the Harbour Phase of INDRA-2026, is the headquarters of which Russian fleet?
x: Vladivostok is the HQ of the Russian Pacific Fleet; INDRA-2026's Sea Phase was in the Sea of Japan.

s: Where was the 5th India-Australia exercise AUSTRAHIND-2026 (19 October – 1 November 2026) held?
x: AUSTRAHIND-2026 was held at the Foreign Training Node, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala; the 4th edition (2025) was at Irwin Barracks, Perth.

s: AUSINDEX is an India-Australia exercise of which service?
x: AUSINDEX is a naval exercise; AUSTRAHIND is the Army exercise and Pitch Black a multinational air exercise.

s: What was the theme of the India-Australia exercise AUSTRAHIND-2026?
o: Joint Mountain Warfare Operations under Chapter VI of the UN Mandate
Joint Sub-Conventional Operations in Island and Coastal Environment under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate
Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief in Coastal Areas
Joint Counter-Terrorism Operations in Semi-Desert Terrain under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate
x: The theme was Joint Sub-Conventional Operations in Island and Coastal Environment under Chapter VII of the UN Mandate.

s: The Indian Army exercise 'Akhand Prahar-II' (October 2026) was held in which district of Rajasthan?
x: Akhand Prahar-II was held in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and followed Akhand Prahar-I.

s: The Battle Axe Division, which conducted Akhand Prahar-II, is under which Command?
x: The Battle Axe Division is under Southern Command (HQ Pune), not South Western Command.

s: SIMBEX-2026, the 33rd edition of which began in Visakhapatnam, is a naval exercise between India and which country?
x: SIMBEX is the India-Singapore naval exercise; the 33rd edition began in Visakhapatnam in October 2026.

s: Under which name did SIMBEX, India's longest-running uninterrupted bilateral naval exercise, begin in 1994?
x: SIMBEX started in 1994 as Exercise Lion King.

s: SIMBEX-2026 in Visakhapatnam was conducted under which Command of the Indian Navy?
x: SIMBEX-2026 began in Visakhapatnam under the Eastern Naval Command, which is headquartered at Visakhapatnam.

s: Between which countries is 'Keen Sword 27', the largest joint field-level exercise in their history, held?
x: Keen Sword is a multi-domain exercise of the Japan Self-Defense Forces and US Armed Forces, held across southwestern Japan.

s: In which year was the US-Japan Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security signed?
x: The treaty was signed in 1960. Keen Sword, the US-Japan exercise, is biennial, not annual.

s: Where was the 11th India-Indonesia Special Forces exercise 'Garuda Shakti 2026' held?
x: Garuda Shakti 2026 was held 27 October – 6 November 2026 at Banyuwangi, East Java, Indonesia.

s: Which unit represented India in Garuda Shakti 2026?
